name: African Violet
hook: African violet not blooming? It needs more light.

steps.title: Bright, cool light
steps.tip: Use a north or east window, out of hot sun. To flower, it needs 14–16 hours of light and 8+ dark.

steps.title: Water the soil, not leaves
steps.tip: Use room-temperature water on the soil, or water from below. Wet leaves get spots. Never let it sit in water.

steps.title: Steady 16–24°C
steps.tip: Aim for 18–24°C by day and about 16°C at night. Keep it away from cold drafts and sudden changes.

steps.title: Humid air, dry leaves
steps.tip: Stand the pot on a tray of damp gravel, above the water line. Don't mist: it marks leaves and invites mold.

steps.title: Feed it lightly
steps.tip: Every 3–4 weeks in spring and summer, use diluted African violet or houseplant fertilizer.

steps.title: Keep the pot small
steps.tip: Repot in spring every 2–3 years. Use a pot only slightly bigger than the roots, usually 10 cm across.

outro: Bright light, dry leaves and a snug pot keep violets in bloom.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension: Growing African violets
RHS: How to grow African violets

faqs.question: Why are there pale spots on the leaves?
faqs.answer: Spots come from water left sitting on the leaves. Water the soil directly or from below, using room-temperature water.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension: Growing African violets
